original.target_description: Study 2; three-condition weight-loss advertisement experiment; PROCESS Model 4 multicategorical mediation of ad type to ad credibility through informativeness, with process simulation and informativeness as simultaneous mediators.

n.sample_role: Study 2 reports 213 MTurk participants; target mediation analytic sample size is not separately printed or explicitly established.
n.quote: In a three-cell, between-subjects design, 213 participants from MTurk viewed one of three ads

replication.target_description: Replication 2 of Study 2; acquired article reports direct ad-credibility comparisons and, in footnote 5, ad-type effects on process simulation. It does not report the requested mediation of ad type to credibility through informativeness.

n.sample_role: 769 participants after exclusions is the full Replication 2 sample, not an established analytic sample for the requested mediation.
n.exclusions: Excluded duplicate MTurk IDs or IP addresses and cases where actual and reported MTurk IDs differed; attention-check failures were evaluated separately.
n.quote: After exclusions, we wound up with 761 participants in Replication 1 and 769 participants in Replication 2

notes: Informativeness indirect-path 95% CIs: progression versus before/after [-.15, .06]; progression versus information-rich [-.11, .11]. Original reports only confidence intervals for these indirect paths; no requested test statistic, indirect-effect point estimate, or numeric p is printed. The Study 2 total of 213 is not asserted here as the target mediation analytic N. Replication d values concern direct ad comparisons, not mediation, so they were not substituted. The narrative success verdict concerns the overall replication of ad credibility; it does not establish success of the requested mediation. Replication source is unpaginated HTML, so section/footnote locators replace supplied p.1. Original PDF title verified against assigned reference; PDF p.9 matches supplied locator.
